summary: 100-foot steel tower in Martin State Forest, Indiana, built around 1932 by CCC crews, removed from active service in 1976 and now a public viewpoint.

facts.design: 100-ft steel tower with an observation deck about two-thirds of the way up

access.note: Register calls it mainly a public viewpoint; the state says short spur trails from the forest trail reach it

visit.trail_note: Reached by short spur trails from the forest trail. Climbability comes only from a hobbyist site, which says it is not in the best shape; the state does not confirm this.

events.note: Newspapers in August 1931 report a 100-foot steel tower delivered at Shoals and to be erected near Willow Hill
Register credits the CCC camp at Martin State Forest with building it in 1932; a county survey quoted by a hobbyist site gives completion in 1933
A brush fire of about 100 acres near Indian Springs was spotted from the tower; reported February 20, 1958
Register: removed from active service in 1976

resolved_conflicts.explanation: August 1931 newspapers report the steel tower delivered and about to be erected; the register gives 1932 for the CCC build; a county survey quoted on a hobbyist site gives completion in 1933. The story reports all three and does not pick one.

sources.title: Willow Valley - Indiana Fire Towers (by Mark A)

notes_for_editor: Build year is disputed: 1931 delivery (newspaper), 1932 (register), 1933 completion (county survey quoted on a hobbyist site). The record has no build year, so none is written to facts. The Living New Deal page refused access (HTTP 403), so it is not cited. The hobbyist climbability claim is not confirmed by the state; the story does not encourage climbing. The DNR page says Martin State Forest was established in 1932 while the hobbyist site says acquired 1933; that concerns the forest, not the tower, and is not reconciled. Current condition beyond the hobbyist note is unknown. Search budget: two websearch.py calls. The 'standing' and 'climbable' notes come from one hobbyist page and are not state confirmation.
